 Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi | Scheme guidelines and implementation guide
Guideline status at 17 November 2026
The PM-KISAN portal currently lists the Revised Operational Guidelines, whose face date is 29 March 2020. The 2020
document is the core published operational text located for this review; use it together with later official updates,
including the Ministry/PIB clarification dated 22 July 2025. Do not treat the 2020 guideline as a newly issued 2026
document.
Prepared as a practical training reference from official government publications and scheme portals. This is a structured summary, not a

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 2
1. Scheme at a glance
Type: Central Sector Scheme of the Government of India, implemented by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers
Welfare.
Purpose: Supplement the financial needs of eligible landholding farmer families for agricultural inputs and household
needs.
Benefit: ■6,000 per eligible farmer family per year, paid in three equal instalments of ■2,000 through Direct Benefit
Transfer (DBT) to an Aadhaar-seeded bank account. The Ministry reiterated this structure in its Lok Sabha reply dated
22 July 2025.
Who identifies beneficiaries: State/UT governments verify land records and eligibility and upload beneficiary details
to the PM-KISAN portal.
2. Eligibility and family definition
  A farmer family is defined in the 2020 revised guidelines as husband, wife and minor children who own cultivable land
 as per the concerned State/UT land records.

 A farmer family is defined in the 2020 revised guidelines as husband, wife and minor children who own cultivable land
 as per the concerned State/UT land records.
 Cultivable landholding is the primary eligibility criterion, subject to the scheme's exclusions.
  The 2020 guideline contains specific land-record and succession provisions. Inheritance due to death is treated
 differently from a later sale, gift or other transfer; the current land-record position and State verification are important.
 Eligibility is not determined merely by occupation as a farmer: landholding records and the exclusion tests must also
 be satisfied.
3. Major exclusions in the published operational guideline
  Institutional landholders.
  Families where one or more members hold/held specified constitutional posts, or specified ministerial, parliamentary,
 legislative, municipal or district-panchayat positions.

 Families where one or more members hold/held specified constitutional posts, or specified ministerial, parliamentary,
 legislative, municipal or district-panchayat positions.
 Serving or retired government employees and employees of specified government bodies/local bodies, subject to the
 stated exception for Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV / Group D employees.
 Retired pensioners receiving monthly pension of ■10,000 or more, subject to the stated employee-category
 exception.
 Persons who paid income tax in the last assessment year.
  Specified practising professionals registered with professional bodies, including doctors, engineers, lawyers,
 chartered accountants and architects.
 Newly added NRI landholding farmer families are excluded under the guideline.
 The exclusions above are a training summary, not an exhaustive legal reproduction. Apply the exact clause wording
and any subsequent government clarification when adjudicating an actual case.

The exclusions above are a training summary, not an exhaustive legal reproduction. Apply the exact clause wording
and any subsequent government clarification when adjudicating an actual case.
4. Registration and verification workflow
Typical workflow:
  Farmer approaches the PM-KISAN portal's New Farmer Registration facility or obtains assistance through a
 Common Service Centre (CSC) / designated State channel.
 State/UT authorities verify landholding details against land records and check the exclusion declaration.
  Identity, bank account and Aadhaar-related details are validated as required by the current portal workflow.
  After State approval and portal processing, payment status and instalment details can be checked through Farmers
 Corner / Know Your Status.

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 3
 If a payment is pending or rejected, identify the exact reason shown in the portal (for example, identity, bank,
 Aadhaar or land-record validation) and route the correction to the responsible authority.
5. Documents and information commonly required
  Aadhaar details and a bank account capable of receiving DBT; the portal may require Aadhaar-bank seeding / NPCI
 mapping.
 Land ownership / Record of Rights / patta or equivalent State land-record information.
  Mobile number for status messages and assisted service.
  Self-declaration concerning the scheme's exclusion categories.
  For succession cases: updated mutation / inheritance land records and supporting State revenue documentation.
 
6. Payment, status and grievance handling
  Check beneficiary status and instalment history through the official PM-KISAN portal's Farmers Corner / Know Your
 Status.

6. Payment, status and grievance handling
  Check beneficiary status and instalment history through the official PM-KISAN portal's Farmers Corner / Know Your
 Status.
 The Ministry's 22 July 2025 reply confirms a portal grievance module handled by State/District officials and the option
 to use CPGRAMS.
 The Ministry also reported the Kisan e-Mitra voice-based AI chatbot, available in Tamil and other Indian languages,
 for scheme queries.
 For training exercises, distinguish 'registered', 'approved', 'payment processed', 'credited' and 'rejected/returned' as
 separate workflow states.
7. What is current, and what is historical?
Core published operational text: Revised PM-KISAN Operational Guidelines, revised as on 29 March 2020. This is
an older publication and must be labelled accordingly.
Later official confirmation: PIB / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, 'Eligibility Criteria of PM-KISAN', posted

an older publication and must be labelled accordingly.
Later official confirmation: PIB / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, 'Eligibility Criteria of PM-KISAN', posted
22 July 2025, confirms ■6,000 annually in three instalments, landholding as the primary criterion subject to exclusions,
Aadhaar-seeded DBT and portal grievance facilities.
Training caution: The 2020 guideline includes historical transitional dates (including the original eligibility cut-off). Do
not mechanically apply those old dates as a new registration cut-off. Refer to the live PM-KISAN portal and
subsequent official instructions for current enrolment, e-KYC, bank validation and correction rules.

 PMFBY | Crop insurance guidelines and claims workflow
Guideline status at 17 November 2026
The PMFBY portal lists the 2023 Operational Guidelines as a current reference. The 2023 document states that it is
effective from Kharif 2023. A Ministry/PIB reply dated 2 December 2025 confirms continued use of the operational
guideline's application-validation and grievance provisions. The 2018 revised and 2020 revamped documents are
historical predecessors, not the best starting point for current training.
Prepared as a practical training reference from official government publications and scheme portals. This is a structured summary, not a
substitute for the original notification, State season notification, bank sanction terms, or current portal instructions.
 Prepared: 17 November 2026

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 2
1. Objective and operating model
PMFBY is a Government of India crop-insurance scheme intended to provide financial support to farmers suffering
crop loss/damage from notified risks, stabilise farm income, encourage adoption of modern agricultural practices and
support continuity of credit to the farm sector.
The scheme is implemented through State/UT notifications, selected insurance companies, banks, Common Service
Centres (CSCs), the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP), and designated government agencies.
Coverage is not automatic for every crop or village: the State notification specifies the notified insurance unit, crop,
season, insurer, sum insured, enrolment cut-off and other local particulars.
2. Who can be covered?
  Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas and having insurable interest in the crop may be eligible.

2. Who can be covered?
  Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas and having insurable interest in the crop may be eligible.
  Owner cultivators, tenant farmers and sharecroppers may be covered where they can establish the required
 insurable interest and provide the accepted land/tenancy/cultivation evidence.
 The 2023 guideline's application validation requires consistency among farmer identity, Aadhaar name, land/tenancy
 proof, insured area and crop actually sown.
 The 2023 framework makes participation voluntary for farmers; do not rely on older descriptions that assume
 compulsory coverage for all loanee farmers.
3. Crops, risks and exclusions
Notified crops: Food crops (cereals, millets and pulses), oilseeds and annual commercial / horticultural crops may be
notified by the State for a particular season and area. Actual availability must be checked in the relevant State
notification.

notified by the State for a particular season and area. Actual availability must be checked in the relevant State
notification.
Insured risks can include: prevented sowing/planting/germination, standing crop losses from specified
non-preventable risks, localized calamities affecting individual farms, and post-harvest losses for eligible crops and
events, subject to guideline conditions.
Commonly excluded / constrained events: losses arising from war, nuclear risks, malicious damage and other
exclusions specified in the guideline; avoid assuming every natural event or every crop stage is covered.
The precise risk package, notification and claim conditions govern. A general scheme description cannot replace the
crop-season notification.
4. Farmer premium contribution
The 2023 guideline retains the standard maximum farmer premium contribution structure below, subject to the
applicable notification and any permitted State/UT support:

4. Farmer premium contribution
The 2023 guideline retains the standard maximum farmer premium contribution structure below, subject to the
applicable notification and any permitted State/UT support:
  Kharif food crops and oilseeds: up to 2% of sum insured or actuarial premium rate, whichever is lower.
  Rabi food crops and oilseeds: up to 1.5% of sum insured or actuarial premium rate, whichever is lower.
  Annual commercial / horticultural crops: up to 5% of sum insured or actuarial premium rate, whichever is lower.
 The balance actuarial premium subsidy is shared by Central and State Governments under the applicable rules. The
State may provide additional subsidy at its own cost where authorised. Premium percentages should not be confused
with the actuarial premium charged to the insurer.
5. Enrolment process and documents
  Check the current season's State notification for crop, area, insurance unit, insurer, premium, sum insured and final
 enrolment date.

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 3
 Apply through the permitted channel: bank / financial institution where applicable, CSC, authorised intermediary or
 the PMFBY Farmer Corner / online facility.
 Provide farmer identity/Aadhaar details, bank account details, land record or accepted tenancy/sharecropping
 evidence, crop and area details, and any other documents required by the State notification.
 Ensure the declared crop and insured area match the actual sown crop and cultivated parcel. Keep the application
 acknowledgement and premium receipt.
 Check policy/application status on the PMFBY portal. Correct errors before the season's validation deadline.
 
6. Claims: event reporting and settlement
Area-yield losses: Claims are generally determined using the notified insurance unit's threshold yield and actual yield,
with Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) and approved technology-based yield estimation methods.

with Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) and approved technology-based yield estimation methods.
Localized calamity / post-harvest losses: Individual-farm assessment and timely intimation are important. Farmers
should report loss through the notified channel within the time limit in the State notification / policy conditions; do not
assume a universal reporting window without checking the crop-season rules.
Prevented sowing / mid-season adversity: These have separate declaration, assessment and payment conditions.
They are not the same as an ordinary end-of-season yield claim.
  Retain the policy/application ID, premium receipt, bank details, crop details, land evidence and loss-intimation
 acknowledgement.
 Escalate non-receipt or disputes through the insurer, district/state grievance mechanism and the Krishi Rakshak
 Portal & Helpline (KRPH), toll-free 14447.
7. Technology, monitoring and grievance redressal

Portal & Helpline (KRPH), toll-free 14447.
7. Technology, monitoring and grievance redressal
  The 2023 guideline covers the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP), digitised land records, CCE workflows,
 technology-assisted yield estimation, application validation and claim settlement.
 The current PMFBY portal advertises Farmer App, WhatsApp chatbot, AIDE, CCE, CLAP and WINDS tools.
  The Ministry's 2 December 2025 PIB reply confirms district and State monitoring committees and grievance redressal
 through KRPH 14447, District Grievance Redressal Committee and State Grievance Redressal Committee.
 For training, teach the distinction between enrolment validation, policy issuance, loss intimation, yield/loss
 assessment, claim calculation and claim credit.
8. Current vs superseded documents
Current core guideline located: PMFBY Operational Guidelines 2023, effective from Kharif 2023.

assessment, claim calculation and claim credit.
8. Current vs superseded documents
Current core guideline located: PMFBY Operational Guidelines 2023, effective from Kharif 2023.
Current supporting evidence: PIB / Ministry reply dated 2 December 2025 refers to the operational guidelines and
current validation / grievance processes.
Historical predecessors: Revised Operational Guidelines (2018) and Revamped Operational Guidelines dated 17
August 2020. Keep these only for change-history comparison; do not train as if they supersede the 2023 version.
Operational rule: A State's latest season notification and crop-specific enrolment dates are essential. The national
guideline does not tell a farmer whether a particular crop/area is open for enrolment today.

 KISAN CREDIT CARD
 KCC | Agricultural credit scheme guidelines and banking workflow
Guideline status at 17 November 2026
A major update is already issued but not yet effective at this reference date: RBI issued final KCC Directions on 19
June 2026, applicable to loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027. Until then, existing KCC instructions govern new
sanctions. The 2026 Directions expressly preserve the extant guidelines for earlier loans until maturity / next renewal.
Prepared as a practical training reference from official government publications and scheme portals. This is a structured summary, not a
substitute for the original notification, State season notification, bank sanction terms, or current portal instructions.
 Prepared: 17 November 2026

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 2
1. Purpose and coverage
Kisan Credit Card is a bank credit facility designed to provide timely and flexible credit for cultivation and eligible allied
agricultural activities. It is implemented through the banking system under RBI directions and related Government
interest-subvention / prompt-repayment arrangements.
Eligible activities can include crop cultivation, animal husbandry, fisheries and other notified allied activities. KCC is a
credit facility, not a grant or automatic subsidy.
A KCC limit is assessed by the lending bank using the applicable State/District Scale of Finance, crop/area,
working-capital needs, repayment capacity, allied activity and bank policy.
2. Eligibility and borrower categories
  Owner cultivators, individually or jointly.
  Tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers, subject to accepted evidence and bank policy.

2. Eligibility and borrower categories
  Owner cultivators, individually or jointly.
  Tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers, subject to accepted evidence and bank policy.
  Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of eligible cultivators, including tenant farmers and
 sharecroppers.
 For allied activities, animal husbandry farmers, fishers/fish farmers and other eligible allied-activity borrowers may
 qualify, including eligible SHGs/JLGs.
3. Credit purposes
  Short-term crop production and cultivation expenses.
  Working capital for eligible allied activities such as dairy, poultry, small ruminants, fisheries and aquaculture.
  Post-harvest and post-production expenses and eligible household consumption requirements under the applicable
 framework.
 Maintenance of agricultural assets and eligible technology / soil-testing / extension-related expenses.
  Insurance premiums where the borrower explicitly consents to funding through the KCC account.

 Insurance premiums where the borrower explicitly consents to funding through the KCC account.
  Investment credit for agriculture and allied activities, such as land development, minor irrigation, equipment, livestock
 and sheds, subject to bank assessment.
4. Application and documents
  Apply at a bank branch or through a bank's permitted digital / business correspondent channel. Ask which KCC form
 and document checklist apply to that lender and borrower category.
 Common documents include identity and address proof, photographs, bank account details, land records / Record of
 Rights / patta, crop and acreage details, and tenancy / cultivation certificate or accepted local-authority evidence
where relevant.
 For oral lessees/sharecroppers, RBI's 2026 Directions permit local administration / panchayati raj certification; where
 such certification is difficult, an affidavit may be accepted for loans up to ■50,000, as specified in those Directions.

such certification is difficult, an affidavit may be accepted for loans up to ■50,000, as specified in those Directions.
 The bank may require a one-time land record / tenancy or equivalent certificate for a fresh loan and a declaration of
 proposed activities at each review, as described in the 2026 Directions.
5. KCC rules in force at the reference date (17 Nov 2026)
The 2026 RBI Directions are final, but the commencement date is 1 January 2027. Therefore, do not apply the
following future rules to a loan sanctioned before that date unless the lender confirms an applicable transition rule.
  For loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027, the 2026 Directions provide a composite KCC facility with six-year tenure.
  Short-duration crop seasons are standardised at 12 months; long-duration crop seasons at 18 months.

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 3
 The crop working-capital drawing limit is built from State/District Scale of Finance multiplied by cultivated area, plus
 10% for post-harvest / household consumption requirements, 20% for specified maintenance, soil-testing, weather
and technology / extension expenses, and applicable insurance premium.
 Marginal farmers (landholding up to one hectare) are eligible for a flexible KCC limit of ■10,000–■50,000 (Flexi
 KCC), based on bank assessment and needs rather than land value.
 Collateral security and margin are waived for agricultural loans including allied activities up to ■2 lakh per borrower
 under the 2026 Directions; above that, bank policy and RBI rules apply.
 The 2026 Directions specify a composite limit including short-term and investment credit components; term-loan
 repayment depends on activity and is generally within six years under that framework.
6. Interest, subsidy and repayment

repayment depends on activity and is generally within six years under that framework.
6. Interest, subsidy and repayment
Do not quote a single universal interest rate as a permanent KCC entitlement. The effective rate depends on the
current Government interest-subvention / prompt repayment incentive instructions, loan category, lender, timely
repayment and applicable RBI directions.
The RBI's 2026 Directions state that banks must follow interest-subvention and prompt-repayment incentive
instructions as applicable from time to time. They do not themselves create a universal fixed subsidised interest rate.
Repayment should follow the crop season and sanctioned facility terms. For allied activities, repayment is aligned to
the activity's cash-flow / income generation pattern.
The borrower should obtain a written sanction letter showing the limit, interest rate, applicable incentives, repayment
schedule, security, charges, renewal date and consequences of overdue status.

The borrower should obtain a written sanction letter showing the limit, interest rate, applicable incentives, repayment
schedule, security, charges, renewal date and consequences of overdue status.
7. Delivery, monitoring and borrower safeguards
  KCC access may be provided through bank branches, business correspondents, ATMs / micro-ATMs / PoS and
 permitted digital channels, subject to lender enablement and borrower consent.
 The 2026 Directions provide for UPI and other permitted digital transaction channels for working-capital credit, with
 explicit account-holder consent.
 Insurance through the KCC account is optional; banks must make available covers known to the borrower and obtain
 explicit consent if premium is debited.
 Banks monitor end-use, review/renew short-term limits and apply their credit and documentation policies.
  Raise service or account disputes first with the lending bank's grievance channel; regulatory escalation depends on

 Raise service or account disputes first with the lending bank's grievance channel; regulatory escalation depends on
 the bank type and the applicable RBI grievance framework.
8. Critical document-status timeline
19 June 2026: RBI issued final KCC Directions for Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks, Regional Rural Banks
and Rural Co-operative Banks.
1 January 2027: Effective date for loans sanctioned under the 2026 Directions. Loans sanctioned earlier continue
under extant guidelines until maturity / next renewal.
17 November 2026 training position: The 2026 Directions are 'issued / future-effective', not yet operative for new
sanctions. Use the lender's currently applicable KCC rules for cases sanctioned before 1 January 2027.
The RBI master-direction page also records that older circulars are repealed in connection with the new Directions. Do
not label the June 2026 text as already applicable before its commencement date.

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 1
 AGRICULTURE SCHEME TRAINING SERIES
 TAMIL NADU AGRICULTURAL
 SUBSIDIES
 State agriculture, horticulture, agricultural engineering and allied scheme guidance
Guideline status at 17 November 2026
The Government of Tamil Nadu's AGRISNET scheme portal displays the 2026–27 scheme year and has fields for
subsidy, scheme description, eligibility and required documents. The Horticulture Department also lists its 2026–27
Policy Note. Subsidy rates and availability are scheme-, component-, district- and beneficiary-specific; this document
intentionally avoids presenting one statewide rate as universal.
Prepared as a practical training reference from official government publications and scheme portals. This is a structured summary, not a
substitute for the original notification, State season notification, bank sanction terms, or current portal instructions.
 Prepared: 17 November 2026

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 2
1. How Tamil Nadu's subsidy framework is organised
Tamil Nadu agricultural assistance is delivered through multiple departments and scheme components, rather than
one single subsidy schedule. The State's 2026–27 AGRISNET portal groups schemes under Agriculture, Horticulture,
Agricultural Engineering and Agricultural Marketing and provides a live scheme/input search.
The AGRISNET scheme interface is structured around: Department → Scheme → Input Type → Component, with
corresponding fields for subsidy, item, scheme description, eligibility and required documents.
The Agriculture Department's portal identifies Uzhavar Aluvalar Thodarbu Thittam (UATT), Collective Farming and
Tamil Nadu Mission for Sustainable Dry Land Development (TNMSDD) among its activities. The exact active
component and beneficiary rules must be read from the live 2026–27 entry.
2. Main categories of assistance to check

component and beneficiary rules must be read from the live 2026–27 entry.
2. Main categories of assistance to check
  Crop production inputs: eligible seeds, planting material, bio-inputs, micronutrients or other notified inputs where a
 current scheme component provides support.
 Horticulture: planting material, protected cultivation, area expansion, rejuvenation, post-harvest and other notified
 horticulture components, depending on the current State/centrally sponsored programme.
 Micro-irrigation: drip / sprinkler systems and related components where notified, with beneficiary contribution and
 subsidy ceiling determined by the current scheme order and category.
 Agricultural engineering: eligible machinery, implements, custom-hiring or mechanisation support under current
 department notifications.
 Water and dryland development: watershed, dryland, farm pond or water-use-efficiency components where the
 district and scheme allocation permit.

department notifications.
 Water and dryland development: watershed, dryland, farm pond or water-use-efficiency components where the
 district and scheme allocation permit.
 Collective / group-based support: farmer groups, FPOs, SHGs or collective farming arrangements where the
 scheme's beneficiary definition permits.
3. Eligibility: practical screening checklist
  Applicant must fall within the beneficiary category defined in the relevant Government Order / scheme guideline
 (individual farmer, small/marginal farmer, women farmer, SC/ST beneficiary, farmer group, FPO, etc., where
applicable).
 Land ownership, lease / cultivation status and parcel details must satisfy the specific component. Do not assume that
 all schemes accept tenants or oral lessees.
 The proposed crop, district, block, area and asset must be eligible under the 2026–27 notification.
  The applicant must meet any category-specific conditions, such as minimum/maximum area, prior asset ownership,

 The applicant must meet any category-specific conditions, such as minimum/maximum area, prior asset ownership,
 water source, technical feasibility, training, group registration or contribution requirement.
 Assistance is subject to budget allocation, target, technical sanction, approved vendor / specification where
 applicable, and availability at the time of application.
4. Documents commonly requested (verify component-wise)
  Aadhaar / identity proof and active mobile number.
  Bank passbook or account proof for Direct Benefit Transfer.
  Patta / Chitta / Adangal / Record of Rights or other accepted land and cultivation records.
  Community certificate, small/marginal farmer certificate, disability certificate or other category proof only where
 relevant to the scheme.
 Quotation, technical estimate, equipment specification, invoice or vendor documents where the component requires
 procurement or asset installation.

relevant to the scheme.
 Quotation, technical estimate, equipment specification, invoice or vendor documents where the component requires
 procurement or asset installation.
 Photographs, geo-tagging, field inspection or completion certificate where the scheme workflow requires them.

Agriculture Scheme Training | Reference cut-off: 17 November 2026
Page 3
 For groups: registration, member list, resolution, bank details and authorisation documents as specified by the
 department.
5. Typical application and disbursement workflow
  Identify the exact scheme component in the current AGRISNET 2026–27 portal or the relevant department portal.
  Check the current subsidy amount / percentage, eligible unit, ceiling, beneficiary contribution, application window and
 district target.
 Contact the Assistant Agricultural Officer / Agricultural Officer, Horticulture Officer or Agricultural Engineering officer
 responsible for the component and confirm the checklist before purchase or installation.
 Submit the application and supporting documents through the channel specified by the department. Obtain an
 acknowledgement / application number.
 Department performs eligibility checks, field verification and technical scrutiny as applicable.

acknowledgement / application number.
 Department performs eligibility checks, field verification and technical scrutiny as applicable.
  Where required, obtain approval / administrative sanction before purchasing, installing or undertaking the activity. Do
 not assume retrospective reimbursement is permitted.
 After completion, submit invoice, photographs, geo-tagging and inspection / completion evidence. Payment is made
 according to the sanctioned workflow and budget.
6. Important cautions for subsidy training
No universal subsidy percentage: The rate can differ by scheme, crop, equipment, farmer category, area, district
and funding source. Always capture the scheme component and Government Order number alongside the rate.
Do not use an old policy note as a current entitlement: Policy notes describe departmental priorities and
allocations for a financial year; they are not automatically the detailed operational guideline for every component.

allocations for a financial year; they are not automatically the detailed operational guideline for every component.
Do not buy first and apply later: Many capital-assistance components require prior application, technical inspection
or approval. Confirm the sequence with the implementing officer.
Budget and targets matter: Eligibility does not guarantee immediate sanction. Assistance may be limited by annual
allocation, district targets and first-come / priority rules where notified.
State + Central convergence: Some State programmes are centrally sponsored or implemented in convergence.
Confirm the funding pattern and beneficiary share in the current order.
7. Where to verify 2026–27 scheme details
  AGRISNET – Government of Tamil Nadu, Department of Agriculture – Farmers Welfare: current scheme catalogue
 with fields for subsidy, eligibility and required documents.
 Tamil Nadu Horticulture Department – Policy & Rules: English and Tamil Policy Notes for 2026–27 are listed.

with fields for subsidy, eligibility and required documents.
 Tamil Nadu Horticulture Department – Policy & Rules: English and Tamil Policy Notes for 2026–27 are listed.
  TNAU Agri Tech Portal – Government Schemes and Services: indexes Agriculture, Horticulture, Agri-Engineering
 and other policy notes by year, including 2026.
 For an actual application, the concerned block / district department office is the final operational contact for local
 targets, current forms, technical conditions and document acceptance.
Department contact shown on AGRISNET: Department of Agriculture, Chepauk, Chennai-05; phone (044)
28583323; email coa.fcms@gmail.com. Verify contact details on the live portal before use.
8. Current vs historical publications
